In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of novel ferrocenoindenes, their synthesis, and their characterization.
the design of chiral ferrocenyl-indenes as ligands for asymmetric metal-catalyzed reactions.
the synthesis of new ferrocenoindenes and their characterization by means of X-ray diffraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ferrocenoindene ligands described herein can be used as building blocks in the design of chiral metal complexes, but that the exact nature of the ligands and the metal center involved will be decisive for their application-oriented use.
ferrocenoindenes are indeed valuable ligands for the development of asymmetric catalysts, and that they are also suitable for further functionalization.

all ferrocenoindenes described in this study are suitable ligands or building blocks for asymmetric catalysis, and the crystal structures of the compounds described herein provide valuable information for the design of chiral ferrocenoindene catalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ferrocenoindene scaffold can be easily modified at various positions, which is an important prerequisite for its application in asymmetric catalysis.
the ferroceno[2]indene core is a valuable scaffold for the construction of planar-chiral ligands.
the synthesis of ferroceno[2]indenes and benzo[1]indenoferrocenes has been achieved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ferrocenyl moiety is a versatile building block that can be used in various ways in order to generate novel ligands for asymmetric synthesis.
the ferrocenyl substituent does not have a significant impact on the reactivity of a given functional group.
the ferrocenoindene framework is a versatile platform for ligand design, and that it is a promising scaffold for the development of novel catalysts.
